title: ServiceNow Fixes Five AI Platform Flaws Enabling SQL Injection, Data Theft and Privilege Escalation
content_md: ServiceNow released security updates for five vulnerabilities in its AI Platform, including two critical flaws that could let unauthenticated attackers execute SQL commands , extract sensitive instance data, and potentially escalate privileges. The September 2026 advisory, tracked as KB3159623 and published on September 24, addresses CVE-2026-86857, CVE-2026-86858, CVE-2026-13016, CVE-2026-86859, and CVE-2026-86860. ServiceNow said it found no evidence that the vulnerabilities had been exploited maliciously in the wild. ServiceNow Fixes Five AI Platform Flaws The most severe issue is CVE-2026-13016, a critical SQL injection vulnerability identified in the ServiceNow AI Platform. Under certain circumstances, the flaw could allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary SQL statements against an affected instance’s underlying database. Successful exploitation could enable attackers to access, alter, or potentially destroy instance data beyond intended authorization boundaries. SQL injection vulnerabilities remain especially dangerous in enterprise platforms because database access can expose authentication information, workflow records, customer data, case-management information, configuration values, and other business-critical assets stored within an instance. ServiceNow has linked the issue to product problem record PRB2036897 and rated it critical using the CVSS v4.0 calculator.
